editorial.marketOverview: Friday's historic Nasdaq and semiconductor liquidation remains the last verified US cash-market benchmark. Monday US futures are sharply positive in early trading, while Asian cash-market responses diverge: Taiwan recovered and South Korea remained down. This combination supports a possible relief rally but not a confirmed three-day reversal.

editorial.marketInterpretation: An oversold futures rally may represent short-covering and stabilization rather than renewed broad leadership. SOX's Friday collapse, weak US breadth and Korean chip stress continue to argue for elevated downside risk. A durable change requires synchronized QQQ, SOX/SMH and breadth confirmation during the US cash session, with falling volatility. Treasury inputs are stale or unmatched: a 29bp indicative spread is not a current yield-curve reading, and percentages must not be multiplied by 100.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: opening rebound is plausible, but observe whether QQQ and chip shares hold gains through the close and whether breadth improves after the 09:45 ET flash PMIs. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence and Dell earnings can test AI-infrastructure demand and rebound durability. Wednesday November 25: PCE, GDP and Beige Book could reset rate expectations and volatility ahead of the US holiday.
editorial.bullCase: US cash QQQ and SOX/SMH sustain a broad rebound; breadth strengthens and VXN/VIX ease, while Tuesday earnings and Wednesday inflation support rate-sensitive growth. Taiwan's stabilization would then be an early supportive signal rather than an isolated regional response.
editorial.bearCase: Monday's futures gains fade after the open, chip stocks lag, and weak breadth persists. Korean semiconductor weakness, AI spending/debt doubts and geopolitical oil risks then amplify the selloff; hot inflation or a more hawkish rates repricing adds pressure.
